exposure: Intrapartum transfer from out-of-hospital birth settings (home or freestanding midwifery unit)
Intrapartum transfer from an alongside midwifery unit
cohort: The study participants were all births transferred internally from an Alongside Midwifery Unit (AMU) (n=74) and births transferred externally from out-of-hospital settings (home or freestanding midwifery units) (n=72) between 2020 and 2021.
finding: Intrapartum transfers from out-of-hospital settings were associated with a decreased likelihood of spontaneous vaginal birth, an increased likelihood of secondary caesarean section, and higher morbidity compared to transfers from an alongside midwifery unit.
mod_finding: Intrapartum transfers from out-of-hospital settings resulted in a significantly lower rate of spontaneous vaginal births and a significantly higher rate of caesarean sections compared to transfers from an alongside midwifery unit.
